document.title: Afghanistan: Evidence Not There to Prove Assertions that Pak Troops Have Been Deployed to Assist Taliban in the North (Islama 005964)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Confidential] No evidence supports claims that Pakistani troops took part in Taliban victories, though Pakistani military advisers may have trained fighters. An estimated 20-40 percent of Taliban soldiers are Pakistani nationals. Bin Laden is mentioned as supporting pro-Taliban Arab fighters from an office in Herat.

persons.name: Colonel Iman (Retd)
persons.role: Pakistani Consul General in Herat (retired colonel), reported to maintain very close links to the Taliban

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Captured Shibarghan on 2 Aug 1998, advanced into Faryab; Herat is its main resupply base for northern forces; about 10,000 troops in the north.

organizations.name: Northern Alliance
organizations.notes: Accuses Pakistan of military intervention; a source said its representatives discussed using the claim as propaganda.

organizations.name: Government of Pakistan
organizations.notes: Denies troop involvement; admits it may have men 'closely monitoring' the situation; does not stop nationals crossing the border.

organizations.name: Pakistan Army
organizations.notes: Accused of leading the charge for the Taliban; possible military advisers only.

organizations.name: Pakistan Air Force
organizations.notes: Accused of ferrying arms-related supplies to the Taliban, e.g. to Maimana airfield.

organizations.name: US Embassy Islamabad
organizations.notes: Author of the cable, coordinated with Consulate Peshawar.

organizations.name: NIMA

places.significance: Recently captured airfield; alleged Pakistani Air Force deliveries and sightings of Pakistani military men.

events.description: Embassy cable concludes there is no evidence for Pakistani troop deployment but possible military advisers and many Pakistani volunteers.
Taliban advanced into Faryab Province in northern offensive.
Taliban captured Maimana airfield in Faryab.
Northern representative met US political officer and alleged Pakistani involvement.
Northern Alliance-affiliated party figure scoffed at reports of Pakistani troop involvement, saying north used it as propaganda.
Northern representative told polOff Pakistani army units were leading the charge; Afghan businessman reported from Herat seeing no Pak troops.
Pakistani official admitted Pakistan may have men closely monitoring the situation and suggested Herat consulate officials may have traveled north.
US Embassy Islamabad cables assessment that evidence of Pakistani troop deployment with Taliban is lacking.

key_claims: Northern factions claimed Pakistani army units were leading the Taliban charge, but the Embassy found no evidence.
The Embassy judged that some Pakistani military advisers may be assisting the Taliban, though this is unproven.
Pakistani civilian volunteers, mainly NWFP and Balochistan Pashtuns, fill Taliban ranks, estimated at 20-40 percent, and neither the Taliban nor the GOP deny it.
Herat is the Taliban's main resupply base for its northern offensive.
Unsubstantiated claim that bin Ladin funds dozens of Arabs in Faryab through a Herat office.
A Pakistani official admitted Pakistan may have men 'closely monitoring' the situation.
